newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea ruling party reverses stand on reforms.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea ruling party reverses stand on reforms.

text.p: South Korea's ruling New Korea Party has agreed with the finance ministry to go forward with financial reform legislation, a party official said on Friday.
"We decided not to ask the government to delay the legislation," the official said by telephone.
He said Kim Zoong-wie, chairman of the party's policy committee, "retreated from his earlier stance."
"The financial reform bill probably will be dealt with in a special parliamentary session in June," he added. "If not completed, the bill is likely to carry over to the regular session in December."
The ruling party earlier said the government needed more time to handle proposals by a presidential panel examining financial reforms in South Korea.

Kim Zoong-wie was quoted as saying on Thursday the proposals contained "controversial issues" such as the central bank's independence, business conglomerates' participation in bank management and mergers of financial companies.

The official gave no reasons why Kim has changed his mind. But local media said the ruling party and the finance ministry had reversed their earlier positions because of unexpectedly strong public criticism.

Late on Thursday, Finance Minister Kang Kyong-shik told reporters he would try to implement financial reform by submitting the legislation to parliament by September at the latest. He gave no details.

The Presidential Commission for Financial Reform has unveiled its mid-term proposals which are due to be presented to President Kim Young-sam by the end of May. The finance ministry is to review the proposal and present implementing legislation to a special parliamentary session in June or July.
